title: Kanban-style prefill allocator and adaptive kernel-fallback for continuous flow
creator: Lin Zhao
description:
Problem: Our continuous batching pipeline exhibits sporadic tail latency spikes under mixed-traffic profiles (short single-turn requests vs long multi-turn streams). These spikes appear correlated with suboptimal kernel choices for attention-heavy sequences and with contention during prefill slot allocation when bursts arrive.

Goal: Implement a kanban-style prefill allocator that separates short/long flow lanes, providing soft reservation and elastic spillover, combined with an adaptive kernel-fallback mechanism that probes faster but lower-precision kernels for burst windows. The combination should reduce 95th/99th percentile latency by at least 20% in mixed workloads while keeping mean cost-per-token within 5% of baseline.

Approach:
1) Kanban-style allocator: maintain lightweight flow lanes (short-prefill, long-prefill, realtime) with configurable ticket counts and soft-margin thresholds. Tickets grant prefill slots; when a lane exhausts tickets it enters spillover mode where it can borrow from a lower-priority lane with backoff. This design is intentionally simple (O(1) enqueue/dequeue) to avoid scheduler overhead.

2) Adaptive kernel-fallback: implement a per-request kernel probe step during admission where the system evaluates a fast-config kernel path (reduced attention-block tiling or grouped-attention kernel) for the first N tokens. If latency and quality signals are acceptable, continue on the fast path; otherwise seamlessly switch to the high-fidelity kernel with state migration. Probing uses sampled micro-batches to limit overhead.

3) Attention hinting and prefetch: expose lightweight attention-shape hints from the API (optional) and use a small prefetcher to warm KV caches for lanes that historically show high reuse.

4) Scheduling integration: admission control prioritizes lanes based on SLA, recent latency, and ticket availability. The allocator also enforces a soft cap on kernel-switch rate per GPU to avoid oscillation.

Success metrics:
- 95th latency reduction >= 20% for mixed short+long traffic
- 99th latency reduction >= 15%
- Mean tokens/sec unchanged within +/- 5%
- Kernel-switch overhead < 3% of total tokens

Testing plan:
- Stage A: Local microbench harness with synthetic mixes (70% short, 30% long; 50/50; 30/70).
- Stage B: Canary rollout to 10% of hosted production traffic with detailed tracing and rollback flag.
- Stage C: Dedicated cluster soak for Dedicated customers under capacity commit workload.

Rollout and configuration:
- Feature gated behind runtime-1.20 flag (kanban_alloc_enabled + kernel_probe_enabled).
- Default conservative ticket counts; expose dynamic autoscale knobs for Dedicated pools.

Risks and mitigations:
- Incorrect spillover tuning can starve long-running lanes: add per-lane SLA guardrails and an emergency preemption policy.
- Kernel probe quality regressions: start with very small probe window and A/B compare logits; automatic rollback threshold if quality degradation > 0.5 BLEU-equivalent (internal eval metric).
- Complexity in state migration between kernels: design probe to keep KV layout compatible or checkpoint small state during switch.

Deliverables:
- Runtime allocator implementation (C++ core + Rust scheduler glue)
- Kernel probe glue and compatibility adapter
- Unit and integration tests for lane semantics and kernel-switch correctness
- Canary dashboard and alerting queries for 95/99p latency, kernel-switch rate, and token cost
- PRD + runbook for rollback and tuning guidelines

Notes: This ticket focuses on the allocator and kernel-fallback mechanism. Follow-up tickets will add ML-driven ticket autosizing and per-customer heuristics for Dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: Kanban allocator implemented and feature-gated behind kanban_alloc_enabled
Kernel probe implemented with seamless high-fidelity fallback
Bench harness shows >=20% 95th latency improvement on mixed synthetic traffic
Canary rollout runs for 3 days with no customer-facing regressions and metrics within thresholds
Documentation and runbook published and linked from the PRD

2026-01-22 Diego Morales: Prototype of kanban allocator landed in feature branch. Basic ticketing/borrow logic implemented; unit tests added for enqueue/dequeue semantics. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3241

2026-01-26 Ava Patel (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria. Requested explicit canary thresholds and rollback signal definitions. Added to PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Kanban+Allocator

2026-01-30 Diego Morales: Kernel probe sketch implemented. Chose grouped-attention fast path with probe window=8 tokens. Initial microbench shows 10% 95p improvement with negligible cost change. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3289

2026-02-02 Lin Zhao: Experimented with spillover backoff policy. Found linear backoff (0.1s increments) prevents oscillation under moderate bursts. Updated design doc. Added dashboard queries for kernel-switch-rate and per-lane queue depth.

2026-02-06 Security Review (notes): No secrets change; however, kernel-switch telemetry contains model logits (truncated). Agreed to redact full logits in Canary telemetry. Security review not required but ops flagged telemetry redaction as action item.
